The problem asks for the exponent $\alpha$ governing the divergence of the second volume moment of the restricted zero cell, $\mathbb{E}\bigl[\operatorname{vol}(Z_o \cap B_R)^2\bigr] \sim R^\alpha$, at the critical intensity in $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space ($\mathbb{H}^d$).

Solution 1 asserts $\alpha=2$. This is only correct if $d=4$.
Solution 2 asserts $\alpha=1$. This is only correct if $d=2$.
Solution 3 asserts $\alpha=d/2$. This is the established result in stochastic geometry for the critical regime of Poisson hyperplane tessellations in $\mathbb{H}^d$.

The exact exponent $\alpha$ is dependent on the dimension $d$. Solution 3 correctly identifies this relationship based on established mathematical results.

CHOICE: 3
